minutes.headline: Board voted to go on record opposing the Lunenburg Water District's expansion into Lancaster, after a long public hearing.
minutes.summary: The board reorganized, electing a new chair, vice chair and clerk, and set liaison assignments. Most of the meeting was a joint session with the Lunenburg Water District commissioners about a plan to extend the district into Lancaster to sell water to a development. Board members and residents raised voting rights, transparency, environmental and permit concerns, and the board voted to oppose the expansion.

public_comment.topic: Asked what happens to the system if the Keating well were contaminated.
Asked about the Hickory Hills well being pumped during the 2010 drought and the effect on the lake.
Questioned the financial logic of using Lancaster revenue to fund Lunenburg infrastructure and urged capital planning.

public_comment.stated_role: member of the building reuse committee
public_comment.topic: Criticized the district for not pursuing local economic growth and for how residents learned of the plan; urged bringing it under town government.
Asked whether the district can cap Lancaster capacity or charge different rates; questioned the financial case.
Sewer Commission chair urged serving Lunenburg first, e.g., Pleasant View residents, and discussed sewer billing with the water district.
Resident presented a petition with 48 signatures to call a special water district meeting to reconsider the March vote.
Hydrologist objected, citing sustainable water management maps and lack of information before the vote.

public_comment.stated_role: Vice chairman of the Conservation Commission
public_comment.topic: Asked about permit review, decommissioning the Hickory Hills well, testing, and involving the Conservation Commission.
Urged stewardship of water and criticized how the district communicated its decision.
Asked the attorney how voters can procedurally call a special meeting.
Resident said Lancaster's economic development has regional value for Lunenburg.

votes.motion: Nominate Bob everol for vice chair
Go on record opposing the expansion of the Lunenburg Water District into Lancaster
votes.outcome: passed (aye; opposed call not clearly heard)

budget_items.what_was_said: Warrants read for accounts payable, school construction, payroll and payroll deductions.
Water district said proceeds from selling to Lancaster are unknown but would go to infrastructure, electricity, reserves and possibly lower rates.
The district paid for an earlier engineering and MIT study on sewage and water effects.

budget_items.topic: Keating well vs treatment vs Fitchburg water
budget_items.what_was_said: District chose the Keating well over treating Hickory Hills or buying Fitchburg water, which would cost about three times its loan payment.
Off-peak metering avoids demand charges; turning on all wells at peak would cost a lot.

budget_items.topic: Quarterly rate revenue and connection fees
budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioner said expanding the district would bring consistent revenue from minimum charges; connection fees came up as a trade-off.
Superintendent said late bills have risen sharply and the district may bill more often.
Sewer Commission had asked the water district to handle sewer billing to cut cost; the district declined.

decisions.decision: Mrs Bertram will take the Conservation Commission liaison role; Mr Alonzo takes the Finance Committee liaison role; the ZBA liaison was left open for further thought.
Water district attorney offered to give the petitioners the procedure for calling a special district meeting once he reviews the statutes.
The water commissioner chair said the district would not resist calling a special meeting and would do so in a timely fashion.
No Select Board meeting next week; next meeting June 2nd.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to go on record opposing the Lunenburg Water District's expansion into Lancaster; the opposed call was not clearly heard.
Water district commissioners and staff presented the plan to sell water to a Lancaster development, and said the proceeds were unknown.
A resident presented a petition with signatures asking for a special water district meeting to reconsider the March vote.
The water commissioner chair said the district would not resist calling a special meeting and would do so in a timely fashion.
At the start of the meeting the board reorganized, electing a chair, vice chair and clerk without opposition.

why_it_matters: The water district sets water rates and decides where its wells and capital money go, so a plan to sell to Lancaster could affect Lunenburg water bills, supply and the Hickory Hills and Keating wells.
The board's vote is a statement of position, and the decision on the expansion rests with district voters, who may be asked to vote at a special district meeting.
watch_next: A special water district meeting: the attorney offered the petitioners the procedure for calling one once he reviews the statutes.
The next Select Board meeting is June 2nd; none is held the week before.
